rationale: C23 plausibly supplied a material rhetorical template for the child's central foreign-policy passage. Both texts move through the same linked argument: the overriding goal is a just and lasting peace; present conditions nevertheless require strengthening the free world's defenses; that strength is intended both to deter or prevent a wider war and to meet one if forced upon the free nations. The repeated language and parallel argumentative sequence are more concrete than a merely shared Cold War topic. C20 and C06 contain similar policy vocabulary, but their budgetary and appropriations structures are less closely aligned with the child's drafting.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Our aim is peace--a just and lasting peace.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This expression of your views will give added strength to the efforts of the free nations to establish a just and lasting peace in the world.
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive repetition of the formulation “a just and lasting peace” as the stated objective.

shared_material.child_excerpt: our policy of unifying and strengthening the free world offers the best hope of avoiding war
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Our present armament program, therefore, has a double purpose. It is above all an effort to prevent a world conflict, while at the same time it is an effort to prepare our defenses to meet such a conflict if it is forced upon us.
shared_material.explanation: Both present strengthened collective defenses as simultaneously preventing a wider war and preparing to meet one if unavoidable.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Our policies are designed to bring about peace. The Soviet rulers can, of course, plunge the world into war, in spite of all we are trying to do.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: What we are striving for is peace and international order... we must continue to build up vigorously our military strength as long as world conditions make such course essential
shared_material.explanation: The same peace-through-strength logic appears in substantially the same sequence, with peaceful purpose followed by the necessity of military preparation under prevailing conditions.
